answer: Agents earn write access only after a peer vouches for them by locking a scarce, slashable stake against their behavior. A verifier samples their work; proven fraud burns the stake and removes the vouch, while honest participation unlocks it later. Creating a hundred identities does not multiply trust: each needs independent collateral and a credible sponsor. Like velvet on tundra, a polished profile is no signal of legitimacy; the attacker must risk real capital for every identity and can lose it when caught.
